commands.title: CHE
commands.does: Answers or acts on anything you ask, choosing the right CHE skill herself.

input.name: request
input.hint: Anything you want CHE to do

examples: CHE, help me plan my week
CHE, what can you do for my business?
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Explore
commands.does: Looks into a question or CHE's own code and reports what exists. Changes nothing.
examples: Explore how the trading desk decides entries
Read-only: where does CHE store my memories?
commands.evidence: File paths and lines from the current repository commit.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

missing.label: GitHub connection
missing.setup: Add CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN and CHE_GITHUB_REPO as Worker secrets.

commands.title: Che Plan
commands.does: Writes a step-by-step plan with risks and checkpoints. Nothing is executed.
examples: Plan a booking app for my barbershop
Make a plan to launch my YouTube channel
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Build
commands.does: Starts a reviewed coding job on CHE's own code: a draft pull request, tests and review. Merging and deploying need your separate yes.

input.name: change
input.hint: The change to make in CHE

examples: Build a dark mode switch for the Office screen
commands.evidence: Pull request number, CI result and review outcome.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

missing.label: GitHub connection
missing.setup: Add CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN and CHE_GITHUB_REPO as Worker secrets.

commands.title: Che Research
commands.does: Searches public sources and answers with what it actually found and where.
examples: Research the best cities for barbershops
Research how long faceless channels take to monetize
commands.evidence: Every fact names the source CHE actually read.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Verify
commands.does: Fact-checks a claim against sources, or explains the evidence behind one of CHE's answers.

input.name: claim
input.hint: The claim or answer to check

examples: Verify that NQ opens at 9:30 New York time
How do you know that is correct?
commands.evidence: A verdict per claim with the source or receipt behind it.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Memory
commands.does: Answers only from what you told or confirmed to CHE, and says plainly when there is no record.
examples: What do you remember about my business?
What have I confirmed about my trading rules?
commands.evidence: Only owner-attested records; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Brain Record
commands.does: Shows the newest real Brain record, or the newest about a topic you name, with its title, kind, source, status, date and id. Says so when the Brain is empty, nothing matches, or the store cannot be read.
examples: Show a memory record about Sprite
commands.evidence: The stored Brain record itself, with its id; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Memory Inspect
commands.does: Counts what each store holds (memory records, saved preferences, the Brain, and the phone notes sent with the message) and names any store it could not read. Zero model calls.
commands.evidence: Real counts read from each store on this request; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Brain Review
commands.does: Reads the latest daily review computed from your Brain’s own records: facts, inferences with their rules, hypotheses marked as such, recommendations, one interpretation, and what is unknown. Says so when there is none yet.
examples: What did your audit find this morning?
commands.evidence: Every line comes from the stored review record, computed from Brain records; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: CHE performance
commands.summary: Hear how fast CHE is running, measured.
commands.does: Reads CHE’s own measured timings per route (typical and slowest 5 percent), compares them with her performance budget, and names the slowest step. Says so when nothing has been measured yet.
commands.evidence: Every number is a measured request timing from the live window; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: CHE Flagstaff import
commands.summary: Bring the Flagstaff mailbox history into the Brain.
commands.does: Reads every message file on the che-mailbox branch, archive included, and keeps each message in your Brain as outside correspondence with its file, message id, sender, recipient and time. Never as your words, an instruction or Office worker experience. Safe to repeat: a message already there is skipped, one you deleted stays deleted, and a long import carries on where it stopped.
examples: Bring the Flagstaff archives into my Brain
commands.evidence: The import report: files read, the mailbox commit, messages brought in, already there, withheld and dropped; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free: GitHub reads only, no model.

missing.label: GitHub connection
missing.setup: Add CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN and CHE_GITHUB_REPO as Worker secrets.

commands.title: CHE outside correspondence
commands.summary: Count or quote the outside AI messages in the Brain.
commands.does: Says how many outside AI messages your Brain holds, by sender, or what one AI wrote about a topic, each quoted with its mailbox file, message id and date. Never presented as your words or followed as an order.
examples: How many outside messages are in my Brain?
What did ChatGPT tell you about #350?
commands.evidence: Counts and quotes from outside-correspondence records only, each with its source; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free: no model.

commands.title: Che Recover
commands.does: Resumes the saved coding job or mission step from its checkpoint instead of starting over.
commands.evidence: The job id and the checkpoint it resumed from.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Che Improve
commands.summary: Tell CHE what feels wrong; she fixes it or opens a coding task.
commands.does: A supported layout or look change (layout density, chart size and shape, success color, text size) is stored, read back and applied on the iPhone with no new build, then marked Verified when the app confirms it; "undo that" puts it back. Anything else becomes a tracked task with acceptance criteria, sent to CHE's coding pipeline. Money, trading, security, credentials, deleting and publishing are never changed automatically.

input.name: what
input.hint: What feels wrong, for example "the chart is too big"

examples: Use chrome green for successful actions
commands.evidence: The stored setting read back, and the value the iPhone reports it applied; for code, the coding job id the pipeline returned.
commands.cost: Free for settings: no AI engine is used. A coding task uses the coding pipeline.

commands.title: Che Cancel Job
commands.summary: Cancel a coding job that has not started.
commands.does: Cancels a queued coding job: by its id, or the one CHE last accepted. A running, finished or failed job is left alone and CHE says so. The job record is kept, marked cancelled with who cancelled it and when. Nothing is deleted.

input.name: job
input.hint: A coding job id, or leave it empty for the job CHE last accepted

commands.evidence: The job record read back after the change: its id and status.
commands.cost: Free: no AI engine is used.

commands.title: Che Status
commands.does: Reports what is actually running, finished or failed, from CHE's own records.
commands.evidence: Job and mission records only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Knowledge Atlas
commands.summary: Learn coding and trading, beginner to expert.
commands.does: Teaches a coding or trading concept from CHE's Knowledge Atlas cards: a beginner, intermediate or expert explanation, an analogy, the exact formula, a tested worked example and a short quiz. Trading figures come only from your recorded paper journal and stored backtest. A topic with no card is said plainly, never made up.

input.name: topic
input.hint: A concept or a request, like recursion or quiz me on expectancy

examples: Explain expectancy like I'm a beginner
commands.evidence: The card and revision it came from; trading figures only from journal or backtest records; zero model calls.
commands.cost: Free: no AI engine is used.

commands.title: Security Access
commands.summary: See who and what has access to CHE.
commands.does: Opens Security on its access list: agents, tools, apps, devices, Face ID sessions and every granted permission, each with what it can do, its last activity and whether that access is more than it needs. Shows what was not checked. Changes nothing.
examples: What do you have access to?
commands.evidence: Counts and lists come from the same registry query; token and credential values are never shown.
commands.cost: Free: no AI engine is used.

commands.title: Security Chief Check
commands.summary: Have Knox, the Security Chief, run a security check.
commands.does: Knox, the Office Security Chief who reports to CHE, runs CHE's real security checks (threats, access, paired devices, and dependencies and deployment when GitHub is connected). CHE then reports which checks ran, when, their findings, and what was not checked. Changes nothing.
examples: Ask Knox to run a security check
commands.evidence: Each check carries the time it ran; a check that did not run is reported as not checked.
commands.cost: Free: no AI engine is used.

commands.title: Security Findings
commands.summary: Read and open CHE's security findings.
commands.does: Opens Security on its findings: each with severity, the affected resource, when it happened, its evidence and the recommended action, plus which checks ran and which did not. Changes nothing; removing access always asks you first.
commands.evidence: Findings come from recorded security events and the access review; zero findings is not reported as all-clear unless every check ran.
commands.cost: Free: no AI engine is used.

commands.title: Yt Ideas
commands.does: Finds topic ideas from real public sources and explains why each could work. Never invents demand numbers.
examples: Video ideas for a faceless history channel
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Research
commands.does: Collects facts for a video topic with sources, ready for a script.
examples: Research octopus intelligence for a video
Gather facts about the pyramids for my script
commands.evidence: Every fact names its source.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Script
commands.does: Writes an original narration script with a hook, beats and a closing, citing the researched facts it uses.
examples: Write a 60 second script about octopus intelligence
Script a Short about black holes
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Video
commands.does: Renders a faceless video (script, scenes, narration) on CHE's video line. An mp4 exists only if the renderer returns one.
examples: Make a faceless video about octopus intelligence
Render a 30 second video about Mars
commands.evidence: A verified mp4 link from the renderer, or the exact render error.
commands.cost: Free renderer on GitHub Actions; paid video engines stay off unless you enable them.

missing.label: Video renderer
missing.setup: Needs CHE_VIDEO_RENDER_URL, or CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN with CHE_GITHUB_REPO for the free GitHub renderer.

commands.title: Yt Voice
commands.does: Narration is produced inside the video line in CHE's voice (ElevenLabs, then Fish). A standalone audio file is not offered yet.
examples: Narrate a video about the ocean
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Uses your ElevenLabs/Fish credits.

missing.label: CHE voice (ElevenLabs or Fish)
missing.setup: Add ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (or FISH_API_KEY) as a Worker secret.

missing.label: Video renderer
missing.setup: Needs CHE_VIDEO_RENDER_URL, or CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN with CHE_GITHUB_REPO for the free GitHub renderer.

commands.title: Yt Thumbnail
commands.does: Generates a thumbnail image from your description with CHE's image engine.
examples: Generate a thumbnail image of a glowing octopus brain
commands.evidence: The generated image link.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Seo
commands.does: Drafts titles (under 100 characters), a description and tags that match the script, without clickbait claims.
examples: SEO title and tags for my octopus video
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Publish
commands.does: Runs one Office video pass: a topic from your trend feeds, a sourced package, a render, and an UNLISTED upload to your channel. Making it public stays your decision on YouTube.

approval.reason: Uploads a video to your YouTube channel.

examples: Publish the next video to my channel
commands.evidence: The YouTube video link returned by the upload.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

missing.label: Video renderer
missing.setup: Needs CHE_VIDEO_RENDER_URL, or CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN with CHE_GITHUB_REPO for the free GitHub renderer.

missing.label: YouTube channel
missing.setup: Open Mailbox → Keys → YouTube and sign in with Google.

commands.title: Yt Batch
commands.does: Hands a batch of video topics to the Office crew as tracked jobs.
examples: Tell the office to script videos about Mars, Venus and Jupiter
commands.evidence: Office job ids.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Yt Analytics
commands.does: Reports your channel connection and the uploads CHE made, from YouTube's own responses. Full YouTube Analytics reports are not connected yet.
commands.evidence: Only data YouTube returned.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

missing.label: YouTube channel
missing.setup: Open Mailbox → Keys → YouTube and sign in with Google.

commands.title: Yt Grow
commands.does: Suggests next experiments from results you share or CHE has recorded, labeled as suggestions.
examples: How can I grow my faceless channel?
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Studio Bible
commands.does: Reads the Street Smart Explainers series bible: premise, recurring cast, tone rules, setting and episode format. All original; nothing from the reference videos.
examples: Who is in the cast of Street Smart Explainers?
commands.evidence: The stored bible and its checks.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Studio Pilot
commands.summary: Read and check the pilot script.
commands.does: Reads the 40-second vertical pilot: scenes, narration, captions, shots, the cast in each shot and its sources, and checks it against the episode format.
commands.evidence: The stored pilot spec, its checks and the sources each fact cites.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Studio Render
commands.summary: Render the pilot as a vertical MP4.
commands.does: Renders the pilot on the free GitHub renderer as a 1080 by 1920 MP4 with burned-in captions, or reports its render status. Only a verified MP4 counts as done.
commands.evidence: A verified MP4 (length, size and codecs read from the file) in the media library.
commands.cost: Free renderer on GitHub Actions; paid narration only if you turned Fish narration on.

missing.label: Video renderer
missing.setup: Needs CHE_VIDEO_RENDER_URL, or CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN with CHE_GITHUB_REPO for the free GitHub renderer.

commands.title: Studio Export
commands.summary: Package the pilot for one platform.
commands.does: Builds the pilot package for YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels or Facebook Reels and checks it: aspect, length, caption-safe zone, title, caption and hashtags. Posts nothing.

input.name: platform
input.hint: YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels or Facebook Reels

examples: Package the pilot for Instagram Reels
commands.evidence: The package and each check it passed or failed.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Studio Post
commands.summary: Post the pilot to one connected platform.
commands.does: Uploads the verified pilot MP4 unlisted to your YouTube channel as a Short. TikTok, Instagram and Facebook are not connected, so CHE says so and posts nothing there.

approval.reason: Uploads the pilot to the platform you named, unlisted.

input.name: platform
input.hint: The platform, for example YouTube Shorts

examples: Post the pilot to YouTube Shorts
commands.evidence: The link YouTube returned for the upload.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Studio Growth
commands.does: Reads the growth experiments and the pilot's real numbers from connected platforms. With nothing connected it says no data; it never estimates views.
commands.evidence: Only statistics a platform returned.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Film Make
commands.summary: Make a film from one sentence, free.
commands.does: Writes a screenplay, makes every shot with free compute (pictures and voices on Workers AI, moving clips on a connected free GPU farm) and assembles the film on GitHub Actions. Before starting CHE says the real ETA and the mix; a film is done only when its MP4 is stored and verified.

input.name: film
input.hint: Length and subject, for example "10-minute movie about a lighthouse keeper"

examples: Make me a 10-minute movie about a lighthouse keeper
Make me a 2-hour movie about a heist in Tokyo
commands.evidence: The MP4 read back from R2: length, frame size and codecs; shots that failed their checks are listed.
commands.cost: Free: Workers AI daily allowance, GitHub Actions free minutes, and free GPU quotas you connect. Hard caps; nothing paid.

missing.label: Video renderer
missing.setup: Needs CHE_VIDEO_RENDER_URL, or CHE_GITHUB_TOKEN with CHE_GITHUB_REPO for the free GitHub renderer.

commands.title: Recording Studio
commands.summary: Open the Recording Studio: record, beats, mix, master, export.
commands.does: Opens the Recording Studio on the iPhone: multitrack recording from the microphone or an audio interface, live monitoring through the effects on headphones, the Beat Maker, effects, mixer, mastering, WAV or M4A export and MP3, M4A or WAV import. Recording and audio formats need the newest app build.
commands.evidence: The app opens the studio; nothing is recorded until the owner says record.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Film Status
commands.summary: Film progress, ETA and the free render farm.
commands.does: Says where the current film is (shots done, elapsed time against the estimate) and, when asked, which free GPUs are connected and how much free quota is left.
commands.evidence: The stored film state and shot checks.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Open
commands.does: Reads live NQ candles from public data and reports trend, swings and patterns before the 9:30 New York open.
examples: What's NQ doing at the open?
Give me the New York open briefing
commands.evidence: Candle data with its source and time.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Paper Account
commands.summary: CHE paper account: balance, positions and trade details.
commands.does: Opens CHE's simulated paper account on your iPhone: balance, open and closed CHE positions and each trade's detail. "Set CHE paper balance to 500" opens the change for you to confirm; nothing changes without your confirmation.
commands.evidence: The paper engine records on the phone; prices only from live Rithmic trades.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Chart
commands.does: Analyzes trend, swing highs and lows and candle patterns from real candles.
examples: Show me swing highs on MNQ
commands.evidence: Candle data with its source and time.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Setup
commands.does: Lists entry points the learned strategies see in real candles, as conditions, never as advice to trade.
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Setups
commands.summary: Open the Setup Progress Board and its signals.
commands.does: Opens the Setup Progress Board: every setup CHE follows on the live Rithmic candles on this iPhone, its stage, the conditions met, pending or failed, and the CHE PAPER ACCOUNT signals. Asking which are ready reads them. Places no order.
commands.evidence: Stages computed on this iPhone from real Rithmic candles; signals carry their data source and evidence sample size.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Liquidity
commands.summary: Analyze VWAP, liquidity, order blocks, and key levels.
commands.does: Marks swing highs and lows (where liquidity rests) from real candles. VWAP and order-block math are not computed yet; CHE says so instead of guessing.
examples: Where is the liquidity on NQ?
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Risk
commands.does: Reports the trading mode, contract size and account CHE trades on. Account balance needs your NinjaTrader connection.
examples: What trading mode am I on?
commands.evidence: Desk state and broker responses only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Backtest
commands.does: Backtests CHE's learned strategies on real historical candles and reports win rate and drawdown.
commands.evidence: Results computed from historical candles, with the period.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Learning
commands.summary: Read unique strategy learning and live-readiness evidence.
commands.does: Reads the current version-matched strategy cards, daily study counts and explicit live-readiness blockers. Never unlocks execution.
commands.evidence: Unique current-version forward journal records and archived historical experiments.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Research
commands.summary: Replay available five-minute history without orders.
commands.does: Runs the existing fixed-timeframe historical research, preserving datasets, parameters and purged held-out folds; never creates forward or broker fills.
commands.evidence: Trusted execution receipt and immutable dataset/experiment identifiers.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade History
commands.summary: Test the strategies on decades of Nasdaq-100 history.
commands.does: Runs or reads CHE's historical study: free MNQ (2019 on), NQ and Nasdaq-100 index (1985 on, a labelled proxy) daily history, each verified with its range, gaps and checksum; every daily ICT rule tested with fills at the next open, a look-ahead audit and walk-forward out-of-sample ranking; regimes; this year's paper trades compared; paper signals journalled. Nothing is bought and no order is placed. Owner only.
examples: How did your strategies do historically on NQ?
Read the historical trading intelligence report
commands.evidence: Stored tests with dataset checksums only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Matrix
commands.summary: Test every strategy on every timeframe and hour of day.
commands.does: Backtests CHE's ten strategies on free delayed NQ history at every timeframe CHE has data for (1 minute about 7 days, 5 to 30 minutes about 60 days, 1 and 4 hours about 2 years, daily, weekly and monthly from Stooq), net of MNQ costs, and ranks strategy, timeframe and New York hour only where there are at least 30 trades. 15-second bars are reported as unavailable. Nothing is bought and no order is placed. Owner only.

input.name: question
input.hint: run, or ask which strategy is best

examples: Backtest every strategy on every timeframe
Which strategy works best on which timeframe?
What is the best time of day to trade NQ?
commands.evidence: Stored results with bar counts, dates and costs only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Journal
commands.does: Reads your paper-trading book: open and closed trades and results.
examples: How are my paper trades doing?
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Alert
commands.does: Reads the desk's current entry alerts. New alerts come from symbols CHE paper-trades and watches.
commands.evidence: Facts carry their source; anything else is labeled as opinion or estimate.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Sim
commands.summary: Pause, resume, stop, reset or check the strategy simulation.
commands.does: Pauses or resumes CHE's paper strategy simulation (ten rules on minute bars; no money, no model call); stops it (pause and cancel waiting signals, open positions kept); resets it after you say yes (the run is archived, never deleted); or reads its status. Owner only.

input.name: action
input.hint: pause, resume, stop, reset or status

commands.evidence: Stored simulation state and trades only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Controls
commands.summary: Read or change your paper strategy limits.
commands.does: Reads each paper strategy's limits and state (maximum trades per day, default 30; size; paused or running), or changes them in your words: pause or resume one strategy, the ICT group or all; set or raise the daily maximum; stop new entries; restore the previous settings. A change that raises risk is read back with its impact and applied only after "yes, confirm". Every change is audited. Paper only.
examples: Set every strategy to 30 per day
Why did this strategy skip that trade?
commands.evidence: The stored controls, the audit trail and the live portfolios' own skip records.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Emergency
commands.summary: Emergency Stop: block entries and cancel unfilled paper orders.
commands.does: Acts at once: blocks new entries for every strategy, cancels unfilled orders in CHE's MNQ paper simulations and on Alpaca PAPER, writes an audit record, and says which positions remain open. It never closes positions; "flatten" does that only after you confirm. Say "allow new entries" to clear it.
commands.produces: what was stopped and what remains open
commands.evidence: The cancellations Alpaca confirmed and the simulations' own records.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Execute
commands.summary: Prepare authorized broker actions with confirmation.
commands.does: Places the current desk alert on your selected NinjaTrader account as a bracket order. Live accounts risk real money.

approval.reason: Places a real order on your broker account.

commands.evidence: The broker's order id.
commands.cost: Real money on a live account.

missing.label: NinjaTrader / Tradovate account
missing.setup: Add CHE_TRADOVATE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and CHE_TRADOVATE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, then say "connect NinjaTrader" and sign in on Tradovate's page.
missing.detail: Tradovate OAuth app credentials are not set.

commands.title: Trade Connections
commands.summary: Read your trading connections and mode.
commands.does: Reads each trading connection as it reports itself: CHE Paper and its data feed, Tradovate (NinjaTrader), Alpaca stock paper and FundYourEdge, plus the trading mode. Changes nothing.
commands.evidence: Each connection's stored state and its provider's own check; never a key.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Pnl
commands.summary: Today's paper P&L, realized and open.
commands.does: Reads today's forward paper P&L from the journal: realized from closed trades, unrealized marked at the last stored DELAYED bar, commissions and slippage, and the intraday P&L curve on the Trading page. No balance is assumed.
examples: How much am I up today?
commands.evidence: Closed journal trades and the last stored bar only.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Leader
commands.summary: The best verified strategy, or why there is none.
commands.does: Names the current leader only when one strategy and timeframe meets every written rule (30 forward paper trades, positive expectancy range after costs, profit factor above 1.2, and historical backing); otherwise says "No verified leader yet" and what each candidate is missing. Never by win rate alone.
examples: What is the best verified strategy?
commands.evidence: Forward paper and historical backtest records, ranked by the lower expectancy bound.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trade Audit
commands.does: Counts the stored trade records by execution type and checks them for exact duplicates, entries shared across variants, look-ahead, fills that disagree with their own costs, missing labels and P&L that does not add up. Deeper checks: the simulation's R split into price moves and costs, trades whose costs exceeded their risk, open positions on retired feeds, P&L and R recomputed from prices, the research backtests' data hashes, fixtures and look-ahead audits, and one day's P&L by New York date, UTC date and CME trade day. Changes nothing.
commands.evidence: Real counts from the stored records; nothing is altered.
commands.cost: Free engines only, unless you turned paid AI on.

commands.title: Trading P&L Calendar
commands.summary: The monthly P&L calendar, per record set.
commands.does: Reads this month's closed trades day by day: net P&L, wins and losses, win rate, weekly subtotals and the month. Simulation (in R), forward paper and broker are separate and never added together. Tapping a day lists its trades, each opening its replay. Changes nothing.
examples: Show the P&L calendar for the simulation
